meta.title: Add Intel/AMD GPU hardware acceleration support for video conversion
meta.body_summary: Add VAAPI-based GPU hardware acceleration for Intel and AMD GPUs in video conversion, with detection, settings, and Docker driver installation.

perf_labels.notes: Copilot added VAAPI hardware acceleration but maintainer found it non-functional on real hardware; PR closed after multiple cycles of changes.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 2703 changed lines across 57 files, this is a medium-to-large feature addition touching backend, frontend, Docker, and documentation. The PR was closed without merge due to unresolved correctness and design concerns.

review_details.concern_detail: Maintainer nandyalu reported that the implementation did not work on his Intel UHD 750 GPU, requested a switch to unified VAAPI for both Intel and AMD, separate per-GPU enable toggles, dynamic device detection, and proper container driver installation.
review_details.performance_claim: Faster video conversion using Intel/AMD GPU hardware acceleration (VAAPI/AMF) with automatic fallback.
review_details.rejection_signals: Maintainer repeatedly requested changes and reported the feature was not working; PR eventually closed without merge.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Hardware-accelerated video encoding in a containerized environment involves complex driver and device integration; the agent iterated on many aspects but failed to deliver a working implementation on real Intel GPU hardware, highlighting the challenge of testing such features without physical hardware.

detection_detail.code_reading: nandyalu reviewed ffmpeg command generation, security warnings, and GPU detection logic.
detection_detail.manual_testing: Maintainer manually tested on Intel UHD 750 and confirmed it did not work, prompting redesign requests.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmark or profiling evidence was provided; maintainer's manual test showed failure.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: After multiple review cycles and no working implementation, the PR was closed without merge.

core_change_summary.description: Added Intel/AMD GPU acceleration via VAAPI and AMF in video_conversion.py, with environment variables, settings, GPU detection in entrypoint.sh, and Dockerfile driver packages. Later unified to VAAPI-only for both GPU vendors, added per-GPU enable toggles in frontend/backend, dynamic device detection, and user group management.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Extensive documentation updates and frontend build artifacts were also changed.
change_trajectory: Initial plan and commit adding VAAPI/AMF code paths and settings.
Added tests, then fixed B108 security warnings in temp file usage.
Updated GPU detection in entrypoint.sh and enhanced documentation.
Maintainer merged main and added many unrelated commits (min/max durations, settings cleanup, logging fixes).
Added separate per-GPU enable settings and frontend toggles.
Maintainer requested migration to unified VAAPI and dynamic device detection; Copilot complied.
Further Docker driver fixes and documentation updates; maintainer manually reported failure.

review_signals.summary: Requested verification that the ffmpeg options are optimal for Intel and AMD GPUs.
review_signals.action_taken: Copilot optimized options with CRF, async_depth, etc.

review_signals.summary: CHANGES_REQUESTED review (body empty); concerns conveyed via PR comments.
Reported B108 insecure temp file warnings in tests.
review_signals.action_taken: Copilot replaced hardcoded /tmp with tempfile module.

review_signals.summary: Requested updates to GPU detection using container entrypoint and documentation improvements.
Requested individual enable flags for each GPU type instead of single hardware acceleration toggle.
review_signals.action_taken: Copilot added per-GPU settings in frontend and backend.

review_signals.summary: Asked whether libva/intel-media-driver packages are needed in Docker.
Reported Docker build failure with GPU packages.
Manually tested on Intel UHD 750; ffmpeg commands not working; requested VAAPI unification and device detection changes.
review_signals.action_taken: Copilot overhauled to VAAPI-only and dynamic detection.

review_signals.summary: Requested reverting to yt-dlp ffmpeg build, separate package installation, group permissions, device detection updates, devcontainer changes, tests, and release notes.
Bot review summarizing changes (no blocking comments).

collaboration_trajectory: Copilot opened PR and made initial implementation.
Maintainer quickly reviewed inline and requested ffmpeg option verification.
Maintainer then reported B108 warnings and requested multiple design changes (detection, separate flags, docs).
Copilot iterated on each request over several rounds of commits and comments.
Maintainer manually tested, found it non‑functional, and directed a full redesign to unified VAAPI.
Copilot implemented requested changes but PR was eventually closed without merge due to unresolved functionality.
